USER RESEARCH SYNTHESIS - PROJECT MERCURY

We ran 24 interviews over 6 weeks (Mar 1 - Apr 12) with users across 3 segments. Here's what we found.

Theme 1: Onboarding confusion - 18/24 mentioned this. People cant find the setup wizard, they get stuck on step 3 where we ask for team size. Quotes: "I refreshed three times thinking it was broken" (P4), "Why do you need my team size before I even see the product" (P11). Severity seems high but we dont know if this actually causes churn or just annoyance.

Theme 2: Dashboard load times - 15/24 complained. Average reported wait is 8 seconds, some say up to 14. Quote: "I make coffee while it loads, not even joking" (P7). This one is tricky bc we dont have telemetry on actual load times vs perceived, and I still need to check with infra team on what they're seeing server-side.

Theme 3: Mobile experience gaps - 12/24, mostly from the field sales segment. They cant edit reports on mobile, only view. Quote: "I have to wait til Im at my laptop to update anything" (P19). This would be a bigger build effort, engineering estimated 5-6 sprints.

Theme 4: Notification overload - 9/24 but very emotional responses. Quote: "I muted everything and now I miss the ones that matter" (P22). Quick fix might be possible but full solution is unclear.

Caveats: We couldnt reach any enterprise accounts over 500 seats, our recruiting bias skewed toward mid-market. Also 3 interviews had tech issues so those transcripts are partial. Budget for Q3 is not confirmed yet, I heard maybe $180k but that could change.

Lena has to pick two themes to fund. She asked for this by Friday.

need an exec summary of this pentest report for Marcus our CISO, he has to decide on remediation budget and one finding has no owner yet

PENETRATION TEST REPORT - ACME CLOUD PLATFORM
Test period: Jan 8 - Jan 22, 2024
Tester: Northwind Security Group
Scope: All external-facing services + 2 internal network segments

CRITICAL FINDINGS (3):

C-1: SQL injection in customer portal login. CVSS 9.8. Attacker could extract full customer DB. Fix: parameterized queries, estimated 40 dev-hours. Cost: ~$12k internal labor. Owner: Portal team (Priya).

C-2: Hardcoded credentials in API gateway config. CVSS 9.1. Found in 3 repos. Fix: rotate keys, move to vault, update 14 services. Estimated 80 dev-hours. Cost: ~$24k internal labor. Owner: Platform team (Ravi).

C-3: Privilege escalation via misconfigured IAM role. CVSS 8.9. Any authenticated user could access admin endpoints. Fix: scope down role policies, add boundary policies. Estimated 30 dev-hours. Cost: ~$9k. Owner: UNKNOWN - this spans the IAM team and the app team and neither wants to claim it.

HIGH FINDINGS (5):

H-1: Stored XSS in comments field. CVSS 7.5. Fix: output encoding, 20 hours, $6k. Owner: Portal team.
H-2: Missing rate limiting on password reset. CVSS 7.3. Fix: add rate limiter, 8 hours, $2.4k. Owner: Auth team.
H-3: Outdated TLS on internal service mesh. CVSS 7.1. Fix: upgrade mesh, 60 hours, $18k. Owner: Platform team.
H-4: Exposed debug endpoints in staging. CVSS 7.0. Fix: remove endpoints, 10 hours, $3k. Owner: DevOps.
H-5: Insecure deserialization in batch processor. CVSS 7.4. Fix: input validation, 35 hours, $10.5k. Owner: Data team.

MEDIUM/LOW: 11 findings, total est fix cost $34k.

Total remediation cost if we fix everything: approximately $119k. Timeline for critical fixes: 2 weeks if we pull people off current work. We havent decided if medium/low can wait til Q2.

Marcus needs to approve budget and figure out who owns C-3.

can you make an exec summary of this for Tomiko our head of ops, she needs to pick between the three options or propose her own

SUPPLY CHAIN DELAY REVIEW - Q1 2024
Prepared by: Procurement Analysis Team

Delay summary by supplier:
- Redwood Components: 23 days avg delay on 8 orders, affecting Model X assembly line. Cause: factory fire in their Taipei facility Feb 3. They say back to 80% capacity but we cant verify.
- Brookshire Metals: 15 days avg delay on 12 orders. Cause: raw material shortage, their supplier in Chile had export restrictions starting Jan 15. No clear end date.
- Pinnacle Logistics: 11 days avg delay on 6 orders. Cause: port congestion in Long Beach, ongoing since Dec 2023. They rerouted 2 shipments through Savannah but that added 4 days transit.
- Acme Fasteners: 9 days avg delay on 18 orders. Cause: labor shortage, they lost 30% of workforce in Q4 and are training replacements.

Total impact: 47 production hours lost, approx $2.1M in delayed revenue, 3 customer contracts at risk of penalty clauses (total penalty exposure: $340k if we miss Q2 delivery dates).

Options:
A) Dual-source everything - add backup suppliers for all 4. Cost: $890k setup + ~15% higher unit costs ongoing. Timeline: 4-6 months to qualify new suppliers. Risk: new suppliers might have their own issues.
B) Increase safety stock to 45 days for critical components. Cost: $1.2M in inventory carrying cost annually. We'd need warehouse space, not sure if our Memphis facility has room or if we need to lease. Timeline: could start immediately. Risk: obsolescence if specs change.
C) Accept current delays, focus on expediting existing orders with air freight where possible. Cost: $560k in air freight for Q2, unknown after that. Risk: doesn't solve root causes, delays continue.

We also have a question about whether to invoke force majeure on the Redwood contract given the fire, legal is reviewing but no answer yet.

Tomiko needs to decide by Apr 1.

need exec summary of this build vs buy eval for Sana our CTO, she has to make the call by end of month

BUILD VS BUY EVALUATION - SEARCH PLATFORM
Project: Replace legacy search for customer-facing docs and internal knowledge base
Date: Feb 2024

CURRENT STATE:
- Existing search is custom, built 2019, 3 engineers maintaining part-time
- Avg query latency: 1.2s, p99: 4.8s
- Index size: 2.3M documents, growing 180k/quarter
- User satisfaction: 34% positive in latest survey
- Monthly infra cost: $4,200

BUILD OPTION (Project Lighthouse):
- Build on open-source search engine, custom ranking, custom UI
- Timeline: 8 months to MVP, 14 months to full feature parity with requirements
- Team needed: 5 engineers, 1 designer for 12 months, then 2 engineers ongoing
- Cost: $1.8M first year (salaries + infra), $520k/year ongoing
- Risks: hiring 5 search specialists is hard, we've been trying since Oct and only filled 2 positions. Key person risk on ranking algorithms. We might not hit the 8-month MVP target.

BUY OPTION (Vortex Search):
- Enterprise search SaaS, used by 3 competitors
- Timeline: 3 months to production with core features, 6 months for all customizations
- Cost: $380k/year license, $95k implementation, $120k/year for additional infra
- 5-year TCO: $2.3M
- Risks: vendor lock-in, they had a 6-hour outage in Nov 2023, their roadmap doesnt include some ML features we want (semantic search, auto-categorization). Contract is 3-year minimum with 8% annual increase.

HYBRID OPTION:
- Buy Vortex for docs search, build custom for knowledge base
- Timeline: 4 months for docs, 10 months for KB
- Cost: $380k year 1 license + $1.1M build + $250k/year ongoing
- Risk: two systems to maintain, inconsistent experience across surfaces

Open questions: We dont know if Vortex can handle our projected 5M documents by 2026, their rep said yes but wont put it in writing. Also unclear if our data privacy team will approve customer data in Vortex's cloud, they have a review scheduled Mar 15.

Sana needs to pick one.

CUSTOMER SUPPORT QUALITY AUDIT - Q4 2023
Audit period: Oct 1 - Dec 31, 2023
Sample: 1,847 tickets (22% of total)
Auditor: Internal QA team + external consultant Maya Chen

OVERALL SCORES:
- Communication quality: 72/100 (down from 81 in Q3)
- Resolution accuracy: 68/100 (down from 75 in Q3)
- Response time compliance: 54/100 (down from 62 in Q3)
- Customer satisfaction (post-survey): 3.1/5 (down from 3.6 in Q3)

ROOT CAUSES:
1) Staffing - we're at 42 agents vs 58 budgeted. 16 positions unfilled for avg of 4.2 months each. Remaining agents handling 67 tickets/day vs target of 45.
2) Training gaps - 29 agents hired in Q2-Q3 received only 3 days training vs standard 10 days. These agents have 2.3x higher error rate.
3) Tool issues - CRM crashes avg 3.4 times/week, agents lose 25 min per crash. Known bug since Sept, no fix ETA from vendor.
4) Process changes - new escalation protocol introduced Oct 15 added 4 steps, avg handle time increased 18%.

PROPOSED ACTIONS:
- Hire 16 agents to fill gaps + 8 additional to handle projected 20% volume increase in Q1. Total ask: 24 FTE.
- Extend new hire training back to 10 days, add 2-day refresher for existing agents. Cost: $45k for external trainer + 2 weeks lost productivity per agent.
- Escalate CRM vendor issue, evaluate alternatives if no fix by Mar 31. Budget for replacement: $180k implementation + $12k/month.
- Revise escalation protocol, remove redundant steps. Can be done internally in 2 weeks.

CAVEATS: Sample might not be representative, we couldnt audit weekends due to staffing. Also the satisfaction survey response rate dropped to 8% in Dec (was 14% in Oct), so scores might not be reliable.

Devon needs to approve or modify the 24 FTE ask. Budget impact is approximately $1.9M annually fully loaded.

exec summary of this incident collection for Yuki our VP Eng, she needs to approve the action plan and figure out who owns the open item

INCIDENT POSTMORTEM COLLECTION - Q4 2023
Compiled by: SRE team lead Ravi
Incidents reviewed: 14

SEVERITY BREAKDOWN:
- SEV1 (full outage): 3 incidents, total downtime 8.7 hours
- SEV2 (partial degradation): 6 incidents, total impact time 34.2 hours
- SEV3 (minor): 5 incidents, total impact time 19 hours

REPEAT CAUSES:
1) Database connection pool exhaustion - caused 4 incidents (2 SEV1, 2 SEV2). Root cause: default pool size of 50 not adjusted for traffic growth. We've grown 3.2x since setting it in 2021. Fix: auto-scaling connection pools based on traffic, estimated 3 sprints. Cost: 2 engineers for 6 weeks = $48k. Owner: Platform team (confirmed).

2) Deploy rollback failures - caused 3 incidents (1 SEV1, 2 SEV2). Root cause: database migrations not reversible, rollback scripts missing or untested. Fix: require reversible migrations + tested rollback in CI, estimated 2 sprints + ongoing policy enforcement. Cost: $32k initial + $8k/quarter for additional CI time. Owner: DevOps team (confirmed).

3) Third-party API rate limiting - caused 2 incidents (both SEV3). Root cause: Vortex API changed rate limits without notice. Fix: implement circuit breaker + cache layer, estimated 2 sprints. Cost: $24k. Owner: NO OWNER - the integration was built by a contractor who left in Nov, no team has claimed it.

4) Certificate expiration - caused 2 incidents (both SEV2). Root cause: manual renewal process, no automated monitoring. Fix: automated cert management with Let's Encrypt + alerts, estimated 1 sprint. Cost: $16k. Owner: Security team (confirmed).

TOTAL REMEDIATION COST: $120k one-time + $8k/quarter ongoing

ESTIMATED COST OF INCIDENTS (lost revenue + engineering time + customer credits): $890k in Q4

CAVEATS: We only have postmortems for incidents that lasted >30 min or affected >10% of users. We dont know how many smaller incidents occurred. Also, the database pool fix assumes our traffic growth rate stays at 3.2x/year, if it accelerates we might need additional work.

Yuki needs to approve the $120k budget and figure out who owns the API integration item.

Prepared by: Facilities + Finance
Date: Mar 2024

4 offices across 3 states

- Engineering (Austin): 28,000 sq ft, lease expires Jun 2026, $34/sq ft, 198 occupants avg
- Sales (Denver): 15,000 sq ft, lease expires Mar 2025, $36/sq ft, 87 occupants avg
- Operations (Memphis): 22,000 sq ft, owned building, book value $4.2M, 143 occupants avg

Total annual real estate cost: $3.8M lease + $620k operations/maintenance = $4.42M
Avg occupancy rate: 38% (post-pandemic, was 72% pre-2020)

PROPOSAL: Consolidate to 2 locations

Location 1 - New HQ in Portland (smaller space):
- 28,000 sq ft in South Waterfront district
- $42/sq ft (higher per-sq-ft but less space)
- Designed for hybrid: hoteling desks, collaboration zones, 8 meeting rooms
- Lease cost: $1.18M/year, 7-year term
- Build-out cost: $890k (furniture, AV, networking)
- Can accommodate ~250 people on any given day

- Add 5,000 sq ft in same building (adjacent suite available)
- $34/sq ft for existing, $37/sq ft for new space
- Total: 33,000 sq ft, $1.14M/year
- Build-out for new space: $210k
- Can accommodate ~180 people on any given day

Memphis: Sell building. Estimated market value: $3.8M (per appraisal Jan 2024), but commercial real estate is slow, might take 12-18 months. Broker fee: 5%. We'd need to relocate the 143 ops staff, some could go remote, maybe 40 would need to move or leave.

Denver: Break lease early. Penalty: 9 months rent = $405k. Or sublease - broker says possible at 70% of our rate, would save $189k vs penalty.

One-time costs: $890k + $210k + $405k (or $216k with sublease) + relocation packages est. $340k + moving costs $95k = $1.94M to $2.13M
Annual savings: $4.42M current - $2.32M new = $2.1M/year

RISKS:
- Austin expansion assumes adjacent suite stays available, landlord wont confirm past Apr 30 without signed letter of intent
- Memphis sale timing uncertain, could carry building 12+ months
- 40 Memphis staff affected, we dont know how many will accept relocation vs leave, could impact operations
- Some executives concerned about losing Denver presence for sales recruiting
- Build-out timeline is 14-16 weeks, cant move before Aug at earliest

Kira needs to decide by Apr 10 to secure the Austin space.
